title: Willow vs Wispr Flow Enterprise (October 2026)
summary: Willow Voice vs Wispr Flow Enterprise (October 2026): shared dictionaries, admin controls, HIPAA BAA tiers, and cross-device support.
body_markdown:
By mid-2026, compliance for enterprise dictation tools is close to parity.[Wispr Flow Enterprise](https://willowvoice.com/) now holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and a signed HIPAA BAA on its Growth plan ($23/user/month monthly, $18 annual) and Enterprise. What still separates Willow Voice and Wispr Flow is speed across long dictations, data-handling defaults (Wispr's model-improvement setting is on by default for Free and Pro, while Willow Voice runs zero data retention on every plan), and adoption visibility across mixed Windows, Mac, and iPhone fleets. Developers prompting Cursor or Claude Code, clinicians, legal teams, and finance teams each feel this differently, and for teams deploying voice dictation at scale, that's the comparison worth making.


**TLDR:**


-


Compliance is close to parity: both hold SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, with signed BAAs on Wispr Growth/Enterprise and Willow Enterprise.


-


Wispr's model-improvement setting is on by default for Free and Pro, while Willow Voice runs zero data retention on every plan.


-


Willow's September 2026 internal benchmark: Willow Voice held 190 to 230ms versus Wispr's 400 to 900ms, with a 95% English zero-edit rate versus 90% for Wispr.


-


Willow Team starts at $10/user/month annual; Wispr Pro is $12 annual and Growth is $18 annual.


-


Willow Team gives mixed Windows, Mac, and iOS fleets shared dictionaries, admin-pushed vocabulary, and adoption leaderboards, while Wispr Flow adds Android support and Notetaker.

## What Is Wispr Flow Enterprise?


Wispr Flow started as a consumer AI dictation tool (covered in the[Wispr Flow review and pricing breakdown](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-review-voice-dictation) ) and now sells team tiers. It covers Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in 100+ languages, a common baseline across[speech recognition tools](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-speech-recognition-software) . Team features scale with the plan: Pro adds a shared dictionary, snippets, and usage analytics; Growth adds SSO with SAML, admin tools, and HIPAA with a signed BAA; Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, and MDM. As a cloud service, Wispr Flow processes and stores customer data in the United States.

### Wispr Flow Notetaker


Notetaker is a separate meeting-notes product available on Mac and Windows. Transcripts and summaries are stored in Wispr's cloud with no customer opt-out, meeting audio is kept for 7 days, and the model-improvement setting applies to Notetaker as well as dictation. For teams that record meetings regularly, those retention and storage terms matter, a different workflow from dictating emails, tickets, and prompts, and worth a separate look before rollout.


## What Is Willow Voice?


Willow Voice is a real-time AI dictation tool, consistently ranked among the[best AI voice dictation software](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-software-mac) available. A developer prompting Cursor or a clinician charting between patient visits reaches for one hotkey (fn on Mac, Win + Left Shift on Windows, both reassignable), and text lands in roughly 200ms. Auto-Dictionary picks up names, technical terms, and internal shorthand without manual setup, and for teams spread across Windows workstations, Mac laptops, and iPhones, shared custom dictionaries standardize vocabulary org-wide while admin controls push changes to every install at once. Willow is SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA compliant with zero data retention on every plan, and paid plans bring 98%+ accuracy with 3x fewer errors than built-in tools. Offline Mode runs on Mac and iOS for sessions without a connection. In Willow's internal benchmarking from September 2026, Willow reached a 95% English zero-edit rate compared to 90% for Wispr Flow. Zero-edit results for all 10 languages are in our[zero-edit rate benchmark across 10 languages](https://willowvoice.com/blog/dictation-accuracy-zero-edit-rate-benchmark) .


Team pricing is $10/user/month billed annually ($12 billed monthly) with shared custom dictionaries, shortcuts, admin controls, and team leaderboards, while Enterprise is custom pricing with centralized deployment, compliance documentation, and a signed BAA. A free plan is also available for individual evaluation with no credit card and no word cap.


## Speed and Latency


In Willow's own internal testing from September 2026, Willow Voice measured about 190ms for short dictations of 1 to 10 seconds, 200ms for 10 to 60 second dictations, and 230ms for dictations running 5 minutes or more (covered in the[Whisper AI vs. Willow fastest voice dictation](https://willowvoice.com/blog/whisper-ai-vs-willow-fastest-voice-dictation) comparison). Text tends to appear almost the instant a sentence finishes, with little waiting and little lost thought while the tool catches up.


The same internal testing measured Wispr Flow at roughly 400ms for 1 to 10 second dictations, 900ms for 10 to 60 seconds, and 700ms for 5 minutes or more. On short dictations, Wispr Flow is fairly competitive. At 10 to 60 seconds, which covers much of typical professional dictation, the gap widens to roughly 4.5x, a pattern echoed in the[Super Whisper vs Wispr Flow comparison](https://willowvoice.com/blog/super-whisper-vs-wispr-flow-comparison-and-alternatives) .


For a developer writing a PR description on a Windows workstation or a product manager filing a sprint update from a Mac, ~200ms lets text land while the thought is still active, while ~900ms can add a perceptible pause after each phrase. Across an org, that stop-start rhythm compounds, and the net gain from voice input can shrink once correction overhead is counted. Quick, accurate text tends to keep the correction loop short.


## Team Deployment and Administration


Wispr Flow's team tiers add ground beyond the individual plan: Pro includes a shared dictionary, snippets, and team usage analytics; Growth layers on SSO, admin tools, and individual usage reporting; Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, and MDM. Even with that structure, a gap remains: vocabulary drifts across machines unless every admin setting is configured consistently, new hires start from a blank dictionary until someone sets them up, and a clear read on who is dictating and how much time it saves takes digging through separate reports.


Willow's Team plan answers that directly, a distinction noted in roundups of the[best AI-powered dictation tools](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-ai-powered-dictation-tools) . Shared dictionaries with spelling overrides standardize terminology org-wide from the first login, admin controls push vocabulary changes to every install at once, team leaderboards show words dictated and time saved per person, and codebase auto-tagging in Cursor and Windsurf pulls project terms straight from open files.


### Cross-Device Continuity for Mixed-Device Teams


Both tools run on Windows, Mac, and iOS, and Wispr Flow also supports Android. For Willow, the same hotkey, vocabulary, and settings follow a person from a Windows workstation to a Mac to an iPhone, with no per-device setup. Offline Mode on Mac and iOS keeps dictation running locally without a connection.


## Privacy, Compliance, and Data Architecture


The two tools take different approaches to compliance. SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA share overlapping requirements but serve distinct purposes, as outlined in the[Vanta HIPAA and SOC 2 guide](https://www.vanta.com/collection/hipaa/hipaa-and-soc-2) , a distinction that matters for compliance-sensitive teams.


Wispr Flow now holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and a signed BAA on Growth ($18/user/month annual, $23 monthly) and Enterprise, so a HIPAA-covered team does not need Enterprise pricing to get there. Per the[Wispr Flow security overview](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/3467817258-security-and-compliance-faq) , Wispr is a cloud service that stores data in the United States. The "Improve the model for everyone" setting (Settings, Data and Privacy) is on by default for Free and Pro, user-switchable there, admin-controlled on Growth, and off and locked on Enterprise; it also applies to Notetaker. Notetaker transcripts have no opt-out, and meeting audio is kept for 7 days, details covered in the[voice dictation privacy and data security guide](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-security-privacy-guide) .


Willow Voice runs zero data retention as the default on every plan, not a paid tier. SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance are standard, and a signed[HIPAA Business Associate Agreement](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html) is available through Enterprise for healthcare organizations. Offline Mode on Mac and iOS keeps dictation off the network entirely.


### Where the Structural Gap Shows Up


For most teams, the gap is not whether compliance credentials exist on paper. It shows up in two places:


-


Data defaults at lower tiers differ: Wispr's model-improvement setting is on by default for Free and Pro and only becomes admin-controlled or locked off at Growth and Enterprise, while Willow keeps zero data retention as the default on every plan from the start.


-


Notetaker storage works differently from dictation-only use: Wispr's Notetaker keeps transcripts, summaries, and meeting audio in the cloud with no opt-out, a distinction covered in the[Willow Voice vs Wispr Flow dictation comparison](https://willowvoice.com/comparison/wisprflow) , and the BAA path differs by price point: Wispr's signed BAA starts at Growth, while Willow's runs through Enterprise, with zero retention already on by default before a BAA is signed.


Healthcare, legal, and financial teams should confirm these details directly with each vendor before legal review.


### How to Set Up a BAA With Wispr Flow and Willow Voice


1.


Confirm the plan first: Wispr requires Growth or Enterprise for a signed BAA, while Willow requires the Enterprise tier.


2.


For Wispr, check that an authorized admin manages the organization BAA through the admin portal, since individual and organization agreements carry different controls.


3.


Confirm which products and settings the agreement covers: organization policies can lock settings such as model improvement and cloud storage, and Notetaker and Scratchpad behave differently under those policies.


4.


Request the SOC 2 report through the vendor's trust documentation, and for Willow, contact the team directly about the Enterprise agreement before rollout.


## When Willow Voice Is the Better Fit


Willow Voice fits teams that dictate long-form for hours at a stretch: clinical notes, PR descriptions, legal briefs, and financial reports. In Willow's September 2026 internal benchmarking, latency held at 190 to 230ms versus Wispr Flow's 400 to 900ms, and the English zero-edit rate was 95% versus 90%. For a full breakdown, see[Wispr Flow vs Willow voice dictation](https://willowvoice.com/blog/wispr-flow-vs-willow-voice-dictation) .


Teams that want leaderboards, a Team plan from $10/user/month, and a mixed Windows, Mac, and iOS fleet under one setup tend to land on Willow. Wispr Flow's compliance gap has closed, so the remaining difference is data defaults: Willow keeps zero data retention on every plan, while Wispr's model-improvement setting is on by default for Free and Pro. Wispr Flow fits better when a team needs Android support, Notetaker, or a signed BAA on a self-serve-priced Growth plan.


## FAQs


### Should my team choose Willow Voice or Wispr Flow Enterprise for org-wide deployment?


Choose Willow Voice for long-form dictation, team leaderboards, admin-pushed vocabulary, and zero data retention on every plan. Wispr Flow also offers shared dictionaries and usage analytics from Pro, so team features alone do not settle the decision. Wispr Flow fits better if your team needs Android support or Notetaker for recorded meetings.


### What is the core difference in how each tool handles team vocabulary?


Both tools offer shared dictionaries: Wispr Flow from Pro, Willow Voice on Team. Willow Voice adds admin controls that push vocabulary changes to every install, custom spelling overrides, and codebase auto-tagging in Cursor and Windsurf, so developers get project terms recognized from the first session.


### Who is each tool best suited for?


Wispr Flow suits teams on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, plus Notetaker for meetings. Willow Voice suits organizations that dictate for long stretches across mixed Windows, Mac, and iOS fleets, with leaderboard-backed adoption visibility and zero data retention by default.


## Final Thoughts on Wispr Flow Enterprise vs. Willow Voice


[Wispr Flow Enterprise](https://willowvoice.com/) has closed real gaps, with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA with a signed BAA, and team tiers now in place. The open questions are how it holds up in long sessions, whether data defaults favor the user (Willow keeps zero retention on every plan, while Wispr's Free and Pro tiers turn model improvement on by default), and whether a manager gets leaderboard-backed adoption visibility across a Windows, Mac, and iOS fleet. Pilot the Team plan from $10/user/month with one team for a week. Download Willow Voice and see how it fits your workflow.
